title: The PCIe fingers will be thin, soft ENIG immersion gold, not the hard gold card-edge contacts normally use.
what: JLC makes gold fingers only with ENIG (electroless nickel, immersion gold): a gold layer about 0.025-0.05 um thick over 3-6 um of nickel, deposited chemically rather than electroplated. Card-edge contacts in PCIe practice normally use hard (electroplated) gold, which wears much more slowly. JLC's 6-layer page lists the finish as 2 uin ENIG, so the thicker option appears to be the standard choice for this board; the order note says only 'ENIG' and does not confirm it.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J6 fingers A1-A49 and B1-B49; ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md, Gold fingers bullet 1; stack-up copper_finish "ENIG".
evidence: jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-gold-fingers: gold fingers only when ENIG is chosen; no hard gold or thickness given. jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-surface-finish: gold 1 or 2 uin (about 0.025-0.05 um), nickel about 3-6 um. jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb: surface finish 'ENIG 2u"'. A JLC blog post (seen only as a search result; the page returned 404) says 6-20 layer boards default to 2 uin at no extra cost. exports/hdmi/stackup.txt copper_finish "ENIG"; the order note gives 6 layers and 'ENIG'.
source: JLCPCB help pages: gold fingers (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-gold-fingers) and surface finish (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-surface-finish); JLCPCB 6-layer PCB page (https://jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb); all read 11 Nov 2026. The PCIe CEM contact plating requirement was not read (document not public); the hard-gold expectation is engineering judgement.
consequence: The fingers wear after repeated insertions, and contact resistance can rise over time. This is acceptable for a lab card inserted a few times.
suggested_action: Confirm 2 uin ENIG on the JLC order page, and record an insertion-count limit for the card.
already_known: V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 460-461 ('choose the thicker ENIG option'), not carried into the V37 note. The reviewer agrees with minor.

title: 210 vias have 0.15 mm drills (10.6:1), and 64 sit exactly at JLC's 0.20 mm inner hole-to-copper minimum.
what: 210 of the board's 991 vias use 0.15 mm drills in a 1.594 mm board, an aspect ratio (board thickness divided by hole diameter) of 10.6:1. 64 of them have the hole edge 0.2005 mm from other-net copper (the DGND pour) on inner layers L2, L4 and L5. Both values meet JLC's published minimums and the capability page gives no aspect-ratio limit, so this is zero margin, not a violation. The remaining risk is plating quality in thin, deep holes and no room for drill position error; the 6-8:1 aspect-ratio guide the order note cites should be checked before it is relied on.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, 0.15/0.25 mm vias at J610-J617 (104), U801-U816 (40), U501 (3), C508 (1) and 62 others; inner layers L2/L4/L5 against the DGND pour, for example HDMI1_JTAG_TCK at (71.6, 143.9) and B64_L11P_GC at (70.38, 106.8).
evidence: Order Gerber ZIP, HDMI_Extension_Board_V37-PTH.drl: T1C0.150 210 hits, T2C0.200 722, T3C0.300 59, all vias, 991 in total. 1.5944 mm / 0.15 mm = 10.6:1. pcbnew measurement of hole edge to other-net copper (pours, tracks, pads, vias) on In1-In4: 0.15 mm vias minimum 0.2005 mm, with 64 distinct vias at that value on each of L2/L4/L5 (192 instances); 0.20 mm vias minimum 0.25 mm; 0.30 mm vias minimum 0.35 mm. JLC: multilayer via minimum 0.15 mm hole / 0.25 mm via; inner via hole to copper 0.2 mm.
source: JLCPCB PCB capabilities (https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities) and JLCPCB 6-layer PCB page (https://jlcpcb.com/6-layer-pcb), read 11 Nov 2026: via minimum 0.15/0.25 mm, inner via hole to copper 0.2 mm, no aspect-ratio limit stated.
consequence: If plating in the thin holes is poor or a drill wanders, opens or near-shorts at the HDMI ports would be hard to find. If JLC flags the vias at file review, the order is held.
suggested_action: Keep the written-confirmation request for the 0.15 mm drill and the 0.20 mm inner clearance in the note and wait for JLC's answer before production; this is prudent, though JLC's published rules do not require it.
already_known: V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md 'For JLC to confirm: 0.15 mm via drills'; V35 ALL_FINDINGS.md line 55 (zero margin). The reviewer agrees with minor.

title: Pin 19 may carry 0.55-0.77 A, but Molex rates it 0.3 A with all pins at 55 C and 0.8 A only at 25 C.
what: Molex's product specification gives two current figures for this Micro-HDMI receptacle: 0.3 A per contact, tested with all 19 contacts carrying current at 55 C ambient with an 85 C limit, and 0.8 A at 25 C with no other condition. On this board only pin 19 carries power, so neither test matches the real use; a single powered contact is usually allowed more than the all-19 figure, so the high case is unqualified rather than shown to exceed a rating. The expected 0.27 A is 90 % of 0.3 A, but the 0.55 A high case and the current-switch limit of 0.63-0.77 A are covered only by the 25 C figure, and the board sits in a closed enclosure with no fan. The files cannot settle this; a Molex answer for one contact at a warm ambient, or a measured pin-19 temperature under load, would.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J610-J617 pin 19 (PORT1_5V ... PORT8_5V), fed by U701-U708 TPS2553 with R711-R718 = 37.4 kOhm; returns on pins 4/7/10/13/16 and the four SH pads (DGND). The same contact at the other cable end: Frontend J3 pin 19 (VIN_5V), MPN 467651001.
evidence: Molex PS-46765-003 rev 9: sheet 1 sec. 4.2, 0.8 A at 25 C; sec. 4.3, operating -30 to +85 C; sheet 2 sec. 5.1 item 4, 0.3 A minimum, all 19 circuits powered, 55 C maximum ambient, '85 C maximum temperature change' (EIA-364-70A); no derating curve. Farnell copy of the 0467651001 datasheet: 0.8 A maximum per contact. exports/hdmi/pads.csv J610: pin 19 PORT1_5V, no other power pins; exports/frontend/pads.csv J3: pin 19 VIN_5V. power_estimate/START_HERE.md line 35: 0.15 / 0.27 / 0.55 A at the 5 V pin. TI SLVS841G eq. 1-3 at 37.4 kOhm: 637 / 696 / 764 mA (630-771 mA with 1 % resistor tolerance). Ratios: 0.27/0.30 = 90 %, 0.55/0.80 = 69 %, 0.771/0.80 = 96 %. Pin 19 alone carries 3.4x (0.55 A) or 6.6x (0.771 A) the per-contact heat of the 0.3 A test, so the hot-spot rise cannot be read from the specification. design_inputs/START_HERE.md line 44 lists '0.8 A connector pin' without the 25 C condition. enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md line 62: closed enclosure, no fan, nothing simulated or measured.
source: Molex PS-46765-003 rev 9 (EC S2011-0455, 2010-11-19), sheets 1-2, secs. 4.2, 4.3 and 5.1 item 4, read from the distributor copy https://static.chipdip.ru/lib/026/DOC027026286.pdf because https://www.molex.com/en-us/products/part-detail/0467651001 timed out; Molex 0467651001 datasheet, Farnell copy (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/1631775.pdf); TI TPS2553 data sheet SLVS841G, eq. 1-3.
consequence: In expected use nothing happens. Under the high load, or with a port held at its current limit, pin 19 at both cable ends may run hotter than Molex has qualified, risking contact wear or heat damage over time; the 0.8 A ceiling recorded in design_inputs is a 25 C figure, so the margin is smaller than recorded.
suggested_action: Ask Molex what continuous current one contact (pin 19, returns on pins 4/7/10/13/16 and shell) may carry at 50 C ambient for a 30 K rise, and whether PS-46765-003-001 changes the ratings. At bring-up, load one port at 0.55 A and then at the switch limit for 30 min inside the enclosure, and measure pin-19 and shell temperature at J61x and at Frontend J3.
already_known: Same underlying problem as the report's existing finding 'The Micro-HDMI pin 19 contact may be rated below the port current it is asked to carry' (hdmi-parts reviewer, minor). Kept because it adds the primary Molex source and corrects that finding's facts: both 0.3 A and 0.8 A are Molex values, for different conditions. The reviewer agrees with minor and does not raise it to major. The reviewer also notes that a premise that the expected 0.27 A exceeds 0.3 A is wrong (it is 90 %).

title: The Micro-HDMI mouths sit flush with the left edge, not 0.70 mm proud, and no left-edge tolerance is ordered.
what: Molex's recommended layout puts the board edge 1.70 mm in front of the front shell-slot centre, so the receptacle face stands 0.70 mm beyond the edge. On this board the edge is 2.404 mm in front of the slot centre, so the board runs 0.704 mm past Molex's edge line and the eight mouths are flush with the edge. The order note already places panel tabs only between shells and forbids any tab stub or burr proud of the left edge, but it asks for +/-0.1 mm routing only on the card-edge tongue, not the left edge. Whether a slightly proud edge stops a plug depends on the cable's overmold (the moulded plastic around the plug), which nothing in the files settles.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, left Edge.Cuts at x 64.676 (y 47.95-157.55); J610-J617 front shell slots at x 67.08, rotation -90, top side; ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md lines 55-59 and 69-71.
evidence: Molex SD-46765-001 rev D1 sheet 5: front slot 1.70 +/-0.05 mm from the PCB front edge, connector front interface 0.70 mm beyond the edge; sheet 2: 2.40 mm from front face to front tab centre, 3.36 mm between tabs; sheet 1: interface point 1.53 mm above the PCB. pcbnew on the V37 board: slots at x 67.08 and 70.44 (3.36 mm apart, matching), drill 0.65 x 1.7 mm; Molex edge 67.08 - 1.70 = 65.38; actual edge 64.676, so 0.704 mm extra on all 8 ports; face at 67.08 - 2.40 = 64.68, flush within 0.004 mm. The order note says the mouths are flush 'within 0.13 mm', taken from the footprint's Fab outline at x 64.545.
source: Molex SD-46765-001 rev D1 (2013-01-10), sheets 1, 2 and 5 (LCSC copy of the Molex drawing). JLC's standard routed-outline tolerance of about +/-0.2 mm is from memory, not read.
consequence: With a routed-outline tolerance of about +/-0.2 mm, the left edge can stand proud of the mouths. A thick plug overmold then may not seat fully or latch.
suggested_action: Keep the placement, and add a left-edge outline tolerance with no positive deviation in front of the eight mouths to the order note. Check that the intended cable seats and latches on the first board.
already_known: Same underlying problem as the report's existing finding 'The eight Micro-HDMI mouths sit flush with the left board edge, and the factory note does not ask for +/-0.1 mm routing there' (hdmi-layout reviewer, note, source given as 'Molex drawing not opened'); also V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (should-fix; second check: accept and add an order-note line). Kept because it adds the primary Molex dimensions. The reviewer suggests minor rather than note.

title: U700 reaches its 125 C junction limit at about 5.3-5.65 A in 50 C air, inside the 5.0-5.7 A high-load cases.
what: U700 is the 12 V to 5 V power module that feeds all eight ports. TI's thermal curves come from a test board with 2 oz copper on all layers; this board has thinner copper and little copper near U700 on the outer layers, so the estimated junction-to-air thermal resistance (RthJA, degrees of silicon temperature rise per watt lost) is about 33 C/W instead of 22.6 C/W. With that estimate the silicon junction reaches its 125 C rating at about 5.3-5.65 A in 50 C air and 5.6-5.95 A in 40 C air. The project's own high case (8 x 0.55 A = 4.4 A) stays at about 97-104 C in 50 C air, but the 0.63-0.71 A per-port cases from another reviewer's load finding (5.0-5.7 A total) reach 110-138 C; none of this is measured.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, U700 TPSM63606RDLR at (124.0, 60.0), top side, set for 12 V to 5.02 V at 1 MHz by R702 13k (RT) and R700/R701 40.2k/10k (FB); net FE_5V feeding U701-U708; PGND pads 17-20 with 12 vias; L1 PGND zones 'U700 PGND centre/input east/output east'; L6 zone 'U700 thermal L6'.
evidence: SLVSGB4B p.12, 5 V / 1 MHz curves: loss 1.41 W at 4.4 A (94.0 %), about 1.8 W at 5.0 A, about 2.3 W at 5.7 A, about 2.67 W at 6.17 A (extrapolated); the earlier 1.6 W at 4.4 A (93.2 % assumed, findings/_raw/hdmi-power.json) was an overestimate. Fig. 7-13, 0 LFM: allowed air temperature about 93 C at 4.4 A, 83 C at 5 A, 70-71 C at 5.7 A, consistent with the EVM RthJA of 22.6 C/W (p.6). EVM: 2 oz on all layers (SLVUC93 p.19). This board (exports/hdmi/stackup.txt): outer 0.035 mm, inner 0.0152 mm. zones.csv: L1 U700 PGND 35.6/15.3/15.1 mm2; L6 'U700 thermal L6' 529 mm2 in 6 pieces. A 6-layer spreading model calibrated to 22.6 C/W on the EVM gives RthJA about 33 C/W (30-38) here (scratch/gap:hdmi-gap2-u700-soa-derating/RESULTS.txt; not re-run by the checker), matching TI's 33.1 C/W for a 4-layer 2 oz test board. TJ = TA + RthJA x P: at 50 C, 50 + 33 x 1.81 = 110 C to 50 + 38 x 1.81 = 119 C at 5.0 A; 127-139 C at 5.7 A; allowed loss at 50 C is 1.97-2.27 W, about 5.3-5.65 A.
source: TI SLVSGB4B rev. B (April 2022): section 7.3 IOUT 6 A, TJ 125 C and derating note (p.6); 7.4 RthJA 22.6 / 33.1 C/W, psiJT 1, psiJB 12.3 (p.6); TSHD 158 C minimum (p.9); Fig. 7-9, 7-10, 7-13 (p.12); 11.1 layout (outer layers preferably 2 oz, at least 1 oz). https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf. TI SLVUC93 (Sept 2021) p.6 (200 LFM recommended above 4 A at above 1 MHz) and p.19 (2 oz on all layers), https://www.ti.com/lit/ug/slvuc93/slvuc93.pdf.
consequence: At 0.27-0.55 A per port nothing happens. If the Frontends draw 0.63-0.71 A each in 40-50 C box air, U700 runs at or above its 125 C rating with reduced life margin, and it will not shut down before 158 C; eight ports held in current limit (about 6.17 A) also exceed the 6 A output rating.
suggested_action: Set the FE_5V continuous budget at about 5.0 A (0.62 A per port) for 50 C air and check it against a measured Frontend current. At bring-up, measure U700's top temperature at 5 A in the closed box (junction is about 1 C/W above the top); if more current is needed, use 2 oz outer copper, airflow or a top-side heat sink.
already_known: Same underlying problem as the report's existing finding 'U700 may run close to its 125 C junction limit at the high-case port load...' (hdmi-layout and hdmi-power reviews, both minor, which assumed 92-93 % efficiency). Kept because it corrects the efficiency and loss figures and gives a current limit against air temperature. Also in inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (should-fix, 'U700 has thin heat-spreading copper') and inputs/hdmi/V37_record/START_HERE.md (bring-up measurement). The reviewer agrees with minor; it becomes major if the Frontend's per-port current is confirmed above about 0.6 A or the box air exceeds 50 C.

title: Pin 19 margin is unconfirmed: the port switch limit nearly equals the 0.8 A contact rating, with no derating.
what: All power for one head stack passes through a single contact, pin 19, of each Molex 46765-1001 Micro-HDMI receptacle. Molex rates that contact at 0.8 A at 25 C; its 0.3 A figure is only the pass level of a test with all 19 contacts powered at 55 C, not a limit for one powered pin. The expected 0.27 A per port is 34 % of 0.8 A and the high case of 0.55 A is 69 %. Still unknown: Molex gives no derating for one contact at 40-50 C enclosure air, the TPS2553 upper current limit (764 mA) is almost equal to 0.8 A, and the chosen cable's pin-19 wire rating has not been checked.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J610-J617 pin 19 (nets PORT1_5V..PORT8_5V), fed by U701-U708 TPS2553 with R711-R718 = 37.4k; return on pins 4/7/10/13/16 and the four shell pads (DGND).
evidence: Molex PS-46765-003 (distributor copy, EC S2011-0455): p.1 section 4.2, 0.8 A at 25 C; p.2 test item 4, all 19 circuits powered, 55 C ambient, 0.3 A minimum (EIA-364-70A). Text in scratch/verify-hdmi-batch0/chipdip_doc.txt. The LCSC and JLC C563878 pages show no current rating today, so the earlier '300 mA' listing could not be reproduced. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: PORT1_5V = J610.19, U701.6, C721, TP701. TPS2553 at 37.4k: IOSmax = 22980/37.4^0.94 = 764 mA, IOSmin = 25230/37.4^1.016 = 637 mA (SLVS841G Eq. 1 and 3, p.16-17). inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md line 35: 0.15 / 0.27 / 0.55 A per port. 0.27/0.8 = 34 %; 0.55/0.8 = 69 %; 0.764/0.8 = 96 %.
source: Molex PS-46765-003 product specification, sections 4.2 (p.1) and test item 4 (p.2); TI TPS2553 SLVS841G section 8 Eq. 1 and Eq. 3 (p.16-17), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps2553.pdf
consequence: Normal use is within the 0.8 A rating. A soft short held at the switch limit (about 0.64-0.76 A) runs pin 19 near its rating in warm air, and an under-rated cable wire would be the weak point.
suggested_action: Ask Molex for a single-contact derating at 50 C and confirm the chosen cable's pin-19 rating. If either falls short, lower the current-limit setting or run a measured temperature-rise test at the switch limit.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md (cable pin-19 check) and V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (0.8 A from distributors, Molex spec not read). The reviewer agrees it is not a blocker; the 0.3 A figure was not considered there.

title: Five cable-facing pins on each Micro-HDMI port (1, 2, 15, 17, 18) rely only on the switch's 6 kV ESD rating.
what: ESD (electrostatic discharge) is the spark from a charged person or cable touching a pin. The TPD4E02B04 arrays protect only the four shielded pairs on each port, at +/-12 kV contact. Pin 1 (VREF) goes straight to a TS3A27518E switch NO pin, and pins 2, 15, 17 and 18 (JTAG) reach NO pins through 100 ohm, which helps; these five pins rely on the switch's own +/-6 kV IEC 61000-4-2 contact rating. Pin 19 is not a real exposure: a 1 uF capacitor at the connector absorbs a standard discharge.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J610-J617 pins 1, 2, 15, 17, 18; U611-U618 NO2-NO6; R640-R671 (100 ohm). Example: HDMI1_VREF = J610.1 to U611.13 only; HDMI1_JTAG_TCK/TDI/TDO/TMS = J610.17/15/18/2 to R640/R641/R643/R642. Pin 19: PORT1_5V with C721 (1 uF) and U701.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: HDMI1_VREF = J610.1 and U611.13 (NO2) only; JTAG nets pass R640-R643 (100R) to U611 NO3-NO6; PORT1_5V = C721 (CL10A105KB8NNNC, 1 uF), J610.19, TP701, U701.6. U801 covers the transceiver and B64_L5 pairs; U809 covers B64_L6, with IO1/IO2 unused where J610.12/14 are open. TS3A27518E SCDS260F p.1: NC/NO +/-6 kV IEC 61000-4-2 contact; section 6.2 p.5: HBM +/-2500 V, CDM +/-1500 V (component-handling ratings). TPD4E02B04 SLVSD85B p.1 and section 8.3 p.10: +/-12 kV contact, +/-15 kV air. Pin 19: 150 pF x 8 kV = 1.2 uC into 1 uF = 1.2 V.
source: TI TS3A27518E SCDS260F p.1 and section 6.2, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ts3a27518e.pdf; TI TPD4E02B04 SLVSD85B p.1 and section 8.3; engineering judgement for cable-facing pins.
consequence: A contact discharge above 6 kV on one of these five pins can damage a TS3A27518E switch and lose JTAG or VREF sensing to that Frontend. Data paths are not affected.
suggested_action: No change for this order; handle cables with ESD care. At the next revision, consider a low-capacitance array on pins 1, 2, 15, 17 and 18.

title: Crystal Y500 is specified for an 18 pF load but sees about 12-14 pF, so it runs about 20-45 ppm fast.
what: A crystal is cut to oscillate at its marked frequency only when it sees its stated load capacitance. Y500 is specified for 18 pF, but two 18 pF capacitors in series give 9 pF, and with about 3-5 pF of board and pin capacitance it sees about 12-14 pF, so it runs about 20-45 ppm fast (worst case with tolerance and temperature about +90 ppm). This is far inside the USB high-speed limit of +/-500 ppm. Opal Kelly's BRK8305 A03 reference, which this circuit copies, uses the same arrangement: an 18 pF-load crystal on the same 18 pF capacitors.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, Y500 (SJK 7U12000E18UCG, LCSC C524717) at (154.6, 57.6) with C503/C504 (KEMET C0402C180J5GACTU, 18 pF) on U501 OSCI/OSCO; OSCI track 10.74 mm, OSCO 8.65 mm, 0.15 mm on L1.
evidence: exports/hdmi/bom.csv and parts.csv: Y500 7U12000E18UCG; C503/C504 18p C0402C180J5GACTU. SJK specification (LCSC link, scratch/hdmi-parts/ds/sjk7u.pdf): CL 18.0 pF, C0 3.0 pF max, +/-10 ppm at 25 C, +/-30 ppm over -40 to 85 C; no motional capacitance given, so C1 = 3-5 fF is assumed. Load: 18 x 18 / 36 + 3..5 = 12-14 pF. Pulling: dF/F = C1/2 x (1/(C0 + 13 pF) - 1/(C0 + 18 pF)), about 22-42 ppm. BRK8305 A03 netlist (scratch/hdmi-signals/brk8305/net.xml): Y500 ABM8-12.000MHZ-B2-T (CL 18 pF, +/-20 ppm, +/-50 ppm stability) with C523/C524 = C0402C180J5GACTU. FTDI FT_000288 v1.82 section 6.3, Figure 6.4, p.55: 27 pF shown as an example suiting many crystals, with the advice to follow the crystal maker.
source: FTDI FT_000288 DS_FT232H v1.82, section 6.3 and Figure 6.4 (p.55); SJK 7U12000E18UCG specification A1 (LCSC datasheet link); Abracon ABM8 datasheet; USB 2.0 specification, high-speed +/-500 ppm; engineering judgement for load capacitance (CL = C/2 + stray).
consequence: The USB clock runs slightly fast but well inside the USB tolerance, as on the shipped reference; start-up margin is slightly lower. USB will most likely enumerate normally.
suggested_action: Record the choice before ordering: keep 18 pF as in the reference, or make a BOM-only change of C503/C504 to 27 pF C0G 0402 on the same pads to centre the frequency.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V37_record/START_HERE.md 'Still open: Y500 load capacitors'; inputs/hdmi/V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md (open decision); V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md. hdmi-parts and hdmi-order agree with minor; hdmi-signals rated it a note.

title: The order note asks for a 30 degree finger bevel; the record cites 20 degrees, which JLC does not offer.
what: The bevel is the chamfer cut on the card-edge fingers so the card slides into the slot. The order note asks for 30 degrees; the project record says the PCIe card-edge standard (CEM) calls for 20 degrees, but this was not checked because that standard is members-only and public sources disagree. JLC offers only 30 or 45 degrees, so 30 degrees is the closest orderable option. At 30 degrees the bevel (about 0.95 mm long) stops short of the fingers, which start 1.40 mm from the edge.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J6 fingers A1-A49, B1-B49; tongue edge y = 162.054, x 110.18-160.48; ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md PCB item 5, line 56 ('ENIG, 30 deg bevel').
evidence: exports/hdmi/board.json: 98 J6 pads, max pad y 160.654; tongue edge y 162.054, so finger tips are 1.40 mm from the edge. Bevel length = (1.594 - 0.5) / 2 / tan(angle), assuming a 0.5 mm flat: 0.95 mm at 30 deg, 1.50 mm at 20 deg. JLC gold-finger help page: available bevel angles 30 and 45 deg; bevel area must be copper-free. Web search found conflicting secondary sources for the CEM angle (20 deg and 30 +/- 5 deg); the CEM itself was not read.
source: PCI Express CEM Rev 3.0 Fig 6-3, as cited in V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md and V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md (not re-read; members-only); JLCPCB gold-finger help page, https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/jlcpcb-gold-fingers
consequence: A slightly steeper lead-in and a slightly harder first insertion. No electrical effect.
suggested_action: Record the accepted 30 degree choice in the V37 record; no board change.
already_known: V36_prefab_fixes/START_HERE.md 'Finger bevel'; V37_record/START_HERE.md 'Still open': finger bevel angle. hdmi-layout rated it a note; hdmi-order rated it minor.

title: Port power follows only U700's power-good, so the FPGA cannot switch, reset or monitor any Frontend.
what: All eight port switches are turned on together by U700's power-good (PG) output, a signal that goes high only while the 5 V rail is inside its window. If the rail falls below about 94 % or rises above about 107 % for more than 120 us, every port turns off at once and returns about 2 ms after PG recovers. The switches' fault outputs only light red LEDs on the bottom side; no XEM pin or header can read them or drive the enable. A hung Frontend can only be power-cycled by pulling its cable or the 12 V input.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, net PORT_ENABLE (U700.13 PG, R703 10k pull-up to FE_5V, U701-U708 pin 3 EN); FAULT U701-U708 pin 4 to D701-D708 (bottom side) via R721-R728 from FE_5V.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: PORT_ENABLE = R703.1, U700.13, U701-U708 pin 3 (10 nodes), no MC1/MC2/MC3 pin or header; R703.2 = FE_5V; Net-(D701-K) = D701.1 + U701.4 FAULT; Net-(D701-A) = D701.2 + R721.1, R721.2 = FE_5V. nets.csv: PORT_ENABLE 10 pads, 162 mm of track. parts.csv: D701-D708 side = bottom. TPSM63606 PG: UV falling 92/94/96.5 %, OV rising 105/107/110 %, hysteresis 1.3 %, 120 us filter, rising delay 1.5/2.0/2.5 ms (taken from TI search snippets; page numbers not re-checked).
source: TI TPSM63606 datasheet SLVSGB4B (April 2022), section 8.3.9 and the PG rows of the electrical characteristics table, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf; engineering judgement.
consequence: Remote power-cycling and fault reporting need a cable pull, and one rail disturbance resets all eight stacks at once.
suggested_action: Accept for this order. In a later revision, route PORT_ENABLE or per-port EN and a wired-OR FAULT to spare XEM pins.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md power note 'Frontend port power cannot be switched or monitored by the FPGA'. The reviewer agrees: note.

title: VIO1 on the XEM8310 defaults to 1.0 V, too low for every port's LVDS outputs and for the U2/U6 and Q1 path.
what: VIO1 is the XEM8310 supply for I/O bank 64, which drives every port's LVDS clock, command and SYNC outputs. Opal Kelly ships the module with VIO1 at 1.0 V, and a new setting takes effect only after a power cycle. VIO1 also feeds VREF1 of the PCA9306 level translators U2/U6 and the gate of Q1A; at 1.0 V, VREF1 is below the PCA9306 minimum and Q1A may not switch, which can leave the 3.3 VAUX switch U5 and the SMBus/WAKE translators off. The ports still get 5 V whatever VIO1 is; the board has a silk reminder 'VIO1 = 1.8 V' but no hardware interlock.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: MC1.1 VIO1 to bank 64 (B64_* pins on MC1); U2.2/U6.2 VREF1; Q1.2 (Q1A gate); pull-ups R14, R15, R25, R33; Q1A drain/Q1B gate net with R30 (4.75k to +3.3V); /VIO_PG to U5.3 EN; test hole J920.2.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: VIO1 = C27, C9, J910.30, J920.2, MC1.1, Q1.2, R14, R15, R25, R33, U2.2, U6.2. Net-(Q1A-D1) = Q1.6, Q1.5 (G2), R30; R30.2 = +3.3V. /VIO_PG = Q1.3, R31, R32, U5.3 EN. U2/U6 VREF2/EN pulled from +3.3VAUX_PCIE (U5 output) through R13/R23. inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc lines 66-67: LVDS on clk_out/cmd_out with the comment to set XEM8310_VIO1_VOLTAGE = 180 and power-cycle; fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc: sync_out LVDS. Board silk 'VIO1 = 1.8 V'. Opal Kelly: default 100 (1.0 V), allowed 0/100/120/150/180, power cycle required; VIO1 range 1.0-1.8 V. SI1922EDH VGS(th) 0.4-1.0 V at 250 uA. PCA9306 VREF1 floor 1.2 V (from TI search excerpts; the PDF text could not be extracted).
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Device Settings, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/device-settings/ ; Powering the XEM8310, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/powering-the-xem8310/ ; TI PCA9306 SCPS113O (Sep 2023) section 6.3 note 1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/pca9306.pdf ; Vishay SI1922EDH document 67192 Rev B.
consequence: With the factory setting the Frontends get no valid clock or commands, and the SMBus/WAKE path may stay off, until VIO1 is set to 1.8 V and the module is power-cycled. No damage is expected, but it is easy to misdiagnose at bring-up.
suggested_action: Make 'set XEM8310_VIO1_VOLTAGE = 180, power-cycle, measure VIO1 at J920.2' the first bring-up step, before connecting Frontends or loading port firmware.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md gate A.4 'set VIO1 = 1.8 V'; inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc mentions the LVDS need; the PCA9306/Q1 part is not recorded. Both reviewers agree: bring-up note.

title: The FT232H bias resistor R507 sits 12 mm from U501 pin 5 (REF), on the opposite side of the board.
what: R507 (12k 1% to ground) sets the bias current of the FT232H's USB transceiver through its REF pin. Common practice is to place it right at the pin, but here it is on the bottom side, 12 mm away, with a 14.1 mm route through two vias. REF is a DC bias node routed mostly between plane layers, so a USB high-speed problem is unlikely.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: U501 pad 5 REF (top, x 157.975, y 56.25); R507 (bottom, pads x 169.89/170.91, y 54.5); net Net-(U501-REF) on L1, L3 and L6.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: U501.5 at (157.975, 56.25) on L1; R507.1 at (169.89, 54.5); straight-line distance sqrt(11.915^2 + 1.75^2) = 12.04 mm. exports/hdmi/parts.csv: R507 bottom, U501 top. exports/hdmi/nets.csv Net-(U501-REF): L1 0.79 mm, L3 10.17 mm, L6 3.13 mm, total 14.09 mm, 2 vias (0.2/0.4 mm).
source: Engineering judgement. FTDI DS_FT232H could not be read (HTTP 403), so no datasheet placement rule was checked; search excerpts confirm only REF = pin 5 with 12k 1% to ground.
consequence: A slightly higher risk of USB high-speed enumeration problems; unlikely to matter.
suggested_action: Leave R507 as is for this order; move it next to U501 pin 5 at the next layout revision if room allows.

title: The recording pair is P/N inverted on the cable, and neither XDC file records which end corrects it.
what: The Frontend puts its transceiver TX N on HDMI pin 3 and TX P on pin 5, but this board takes pin 3 to the XEM receiver's P input, so a straight cable inverts the data. The Frontend schematic says its gateware must set TXPOLARITY = 1 to undo this, but neither constraint file (XDC, the FPGA pin and timing file) mentions polarity. If both ends or neither end invert, the data arrives inverted. With plain 8b/10b that gives decode errors and no link; a protocol with automatic polarity detection, such as Aurora 8B/10B, would hide it (from memory, not checked).
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: J610-J617 pin 3 through C745, C747 ... C759 to MC3 MGT_RXP (for example J610.3 to C745 to MC3.1, J611 to C747 to MC3.5, J617 to C759 to MC3.53). Frontend: J3.3 = GTP_TX0_N (U1 H1), J3.5 = GTP_TX0_P (U1 H2); symbol pins still labelled TX0_REC_P_3 / TX0_REC_N_5.
evidence: exports/frontend/netlist.xml: GTP_TX0_N = J3.3 (pin function TX0_REC_P_3) + U1.H1 MGTPTXN0_216; GTP_TX0_P = J3.5 + U1.H2. exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: MGT_RXP0_224 = J610.3, C745.1, U801; Net-(MC3-MGT_RXP0_224) = C745.2 + MC3.1; same pattern on all eight ports. grep -i polar in inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/*.xdc and inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: no hits. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/project/Artix_Frontend_8L_V3.kicad_sch line 14885, V42 note: gateware must set TXPOLARITY = 1.
source: Engineering judgement (firmware/hardware contract).
consequence: If the polarity is corrected at both ends or at neither, the recording link is likely not to come up; the exact effect depends on the link protocol, which is not yet defined.
suggested_action: Add one comment line to fit_pins_V34.xdc and Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc: 'rec pair inverted on cable; Frontend sets TXPOLARITY=1; XEM keeps RXPOLARITY=0'.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (interfaces and cross-board notes); the reviewer agrees with note.

title: The SYNC constraint file comment is stale, and ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 leave the Frontend SYNC input undriven.
what: fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc still says the Frontend V40 routes pins 12/14 to its transceiver input and warns not to drive sync_out. Frontend V46 actually receives 12/14 as an LVDS input on B9/A9 with a 100 ohm resistor R64. This board drives 12/14 only on ports 3-6; on ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 the pins are unconnected, so the Frontend input sees only R64 with no failsafe bias (a bias that holds an idle receiver at a known level), and its output is undefined and may toggle on noise. One Frontend bitstream serves every port, and the Frontend has no port-number strap to tell which port it is on.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: J610, J611, J616, J617 pins 12/14 unconnected; J612-J615 pins 12/14 driven from MC1 49/51, 53/55, 50/52, 54/56 through U811-U814; inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc lines 3-4. Frontend: U1 B9/A9 (bank 15, LVDS_25, DIFF_TERM FALSE), R64, U18.
evidence: exports/hdmi/netlist.xml: unconnected-(J610/J611/J616/J617-SYNC_P-Pad12) and (SYNC_N-Pad14). exports/frontend/netlist.xml: /CABLE_SYNC_P = J3.12, R64.1, U1.B9, U18; /CABLE_SYNC_N = J3.14, R64.2, U1.A9. inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 116-117. fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc lines 3-4 still describe the V40 routing to GTP RX0 (E4/E3). The Frontend schematic V41/V44 notes say firmware must use the SYNC folded into 9/11 and that no port-number strap exists.
source: Engineering judgement; inputs/frontend/V2_review_fixes/Frontend_V46_pins_V2.xdc lines 116-117.
consequence: Following the stale comment loses only the optional separate SYNC on ports 3-6, since they also carry SYNC on 9/11. If the Frontend firmware trusts 12/14 by default, stacks on ports 1, 2, 7 and 8 may see false SYNC events.
suggested_action: Update the comment in fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc to Frontend V46 (B9/A9, R64). Have the Frontend firmware use the SYNC on 9/11 by default and use 12/14 only when it sees valid activity.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md ('Outdated warning in the SYNC constraint file'); the reviewer agrees with note.

title: Header J910 mixes 1.8 V bank-64 holes with VIO2 bank-84 holes, and the silk does not give each bank's voltage.
what: J910 puts bank 64 I/O (an HP bank, 1.90 V maximum, powered by VIO1) beside bank 84 I/O (an HD bank, up to 3.40 V, powered by VIO2), and it also brings out VIO2, VREF1, VBATT and VIO1. A jumper from VIO2 at 3.3 V to a bank 64 hole would over-drive that bank. VBATT is tied to ground on the module through a 0 ohm resistor, and on modules built with C1 fitted (PCN-10166) VREF1 has 1 kohm to ground. The back silk already names the bank of each hole but not its voltage.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J910: pins 1-7, 10, 20 bank 64; pins 9, 11-16, 18, 19, 21-26, 28 bank 84; 8 VREF1; 17 VIO2; 27 VBATT; 29 DGND; 30 VIO1. B.SilkS legend above J910 (y 133.62).
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv J910 rows: 1 B64_L12P_GC, 2 B64_T1U_N12, 3 B64_L14P_GC, 4 B64_L12N_GC, 5 B64_T0U_N12, 6 B64_L14N_GC, 7 B64_L20P, 8 VREF1, 10 B64_T3U_N12, 20 B64_T2U_N12, 17 VIO2, 27 VBATT, 29 DGND, 30 VIO1, the rest B84_*. VREF1 = J910.8 + MC1.4 only; VBATT = J910.27 + MC1.79 only; VIO2 = J910.17, J920.9, MC1.80. inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/header_pins_V34.xdc confirms the banks. Back silk shows bank-coded names ('1 64L12P*', '9 84L1P', '17 VIO2', '27 VBATT'). A 1.8 V jumper into VREF1 draws about 1.8 mA.
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Expansion Connectors, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/expansion-connectors/ ; Opal Kelly PCN-10166 (14 June 2023), https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/product-lifecycle/pcn-10166/
consequence: A bench wiring error can over-drive bank 64 or short a battery or reference source to ground.
suggested_action: Add the bank voltage per row (bank 64 = VIO1 up to 1.8 V, bank 84 = VIO2) to the board's START_HERE now and to the silk legend at the next revision.

title: Pins 6/8 carry a 32 MHz clock, not 125 MHz, and the recording link runs on two separate 125 MHz oscillators.
what: The system description calls pins 6/8 a 125 MHz clock pair, but the files and the board silk make it a 32 MHz LVDS forwarded clock. The Frontend transmitter uses its own 125 MHz oscillator Y1, and the XEM receivers use the module's own 125 MHz oscillator; nothing locks the two together. The link is therefore plesiochronous: two clocks with the same nominal rate that drift by their ppm error. The receive firmware (or the Frontend transmit side, if its data runs on the forwarded 32 MHz) needs clock correction or idle insertion plus an elastic FIFO.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: MC1 clk_out pins (bank 64) to J610-J617 pins 6/8; XEM rec_refclk V7/V6. Frontend: Y1 through C78/C79 to U1 B6/B5 (MGTREFCLK1_216); J3.6/8 = /CABLE_CLK_P/N on general-purpose I/O.
evidence: inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc line 4 ('HDMI 6/8 clk_out[k] 32 MHz forwarded clock, LVDS, bank 64'), lines 63-64 (rec_refclk V7/V6, XEM on-module 125 MHz oscillator), line 71 create_clock 8.000 ns. HDMI board F.SilkS '32 MHz clock out (LVDS)'. exports/frontend/pads.csv: Y1.4/5 OSC125_P/N (AX3DAF1-125.0000T3) to C78.1/C79.1; C78.2/C79.2 GTP_REFCLK1_P/N to U1 B6/B5. Slip rate example: at 100 ppm combined, about one word in 10,000; actual oscillator stability not confirmed (AX3 datasheet did not render; Opal Kelly gives no ppm figure).
source: Opal Kelly XEM8310 Clock Oscillators, https://docs.opalkelly.com/xem8310/clock-oscillators/ ; engineering judgement.
consequence: If the firmware assumes a synchronous link, data slips at a rate set by the two oscillators' frequency error.
suggested_action: Correct the system record to say pins 6/8 carry 32 MHz. Use a protocol with clock correction, or cross into the receive clock domain through an elastic FIFO.

title: WAKE#, SMDAT and SMCLK are left unconstrained, so Vivado's default pull-down can hold PCIe WAKE# low.
what: WAKE# is the PCIe line a card pulls low to ask the host to wake up; SMDAT and SMCLK are the slot's SMBus (a slow two-wire management bus). All three reach FPGA bank 64 through 0 ohm resistors, and the pin constraint file leaves them unconstrained on purpose, so Vivado gives them its default internal pull-down. WAKE# has only a weak 100 kohm pull-up on the FPGA side (about 18 uA at 1.8 V), so the pull-down can hold it low, and level shifter U6 passes that low to the slot. SMCLK and SMDAT have stronger 4.75 kohm pull-ups, so they are not held low and see only a small extra load.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: R9 -> MC1.40, ball AB19 (B64_L20N, /PCIE_WAKE_B_VIO); R10 -> MC1.42, AE17 (B64_L17P, /PCIE_SMDAT_VIO); R11 -> MC1.44, AF17 (B64_L17N, /PCIE_SMCLK_VIO); R25 100 kohm WAKE_B_VIO to VIO1; R14, R15 to VIO1; U6 PCA9306 pin 3 WAKE_B_VIO to pin 6 /PCIE_WAKE_B_3V3 = J6.B11, TP16; U2 PCA9306 to J6.B5/B6.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: R9 /PCIE_WAKE_B_VIO to B64_L20N, R10 /PCIE_SMDAT_VIO to B64_L17P, R11 /PCIE_SMCLK_VIO to B64_L17N; R25 100 kohm to VIO1; R14/R15 4.75 kohm to VIO1 (value per the V35 review); U6 pin 6 = J6.B11. inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34.xdc lines 75-78: 'Not constrained here, on purpose'. Pull-up current 1.8 V / 100 kohm = 18 uA. The pull-down current of the FPGA pins was not re-read from the data sheet.
source: AMD UG908 (2023.1), Vivado Programming and Debugging, bitstream settings for Artix/Kintex/Virtex UltraScale devices: BITSTREAM.CONFIG.UNUSEDPIN default Pulldown (seen in AMD documentation search results; the page itself returned 404). Engineering judgement for the effect at the slot.
consequence: In a PC slot (J6), a host with a weak WAKE# pull-up may see a constant wake request. In normal running (S0) WAKE# is usually ignored.
suggested_action: Add the three ports to the XDC as LVCMOS18 inputs with no pull, or set BITSTREAM.CONFIG.UNUSEDPIN to Pullnone.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md ('PCIe sideband pins are populated but left unconstrained'); the reviewer agrees with note.

title: Frontend JTAG TMS runs on Micro-HDMI pin 2 (Utility), a wire some cables do not connect.
what: On every port, pin 2 of the Micro-HDMI (Type D) connector carries the JTAG TMS line to the Frontend. HDMI calls pin 2 the Utility (HEAC+) pin; it was reserved before HDMI 1.4 and is needed only for the Ethernet and Audio Return channel, so some cables may leave it unwired. Pin 15 (the HDMI CEC pin, here TDI) is also sometimes left out of cheap cables. If pin 2 is open, JTAG to that Frontend fails while power and data links still work; the board files cannot settle this, only a continuity test of the actual cables can.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, J610-J617: pin 1 HDMIn_VREF, pin 2 HDMIn_JTAG_TMS (e.g. HDMI1_JTAG_TMS = J610.2, R642.2), pin 15 TDI, 17 TCK, 18 TDO, 19 PORTn_5V. Frontend FPGA Board J3.2 FPGA_JTAG_TMS.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: the J610-J617 pin assignments above; HDMI1_JTAG_TMS on J610.2 and R642.2. exports/frontend/pads.csv: J3.2 FPGA_JTAG_TMS. Public HDMI pinout summaries state the Utility conductor (Type A pin 14, Type D pin 2) is optional for HEAC in HDMI 1.4 and later; a cable-quality application note lists a missing pin 14 among cable defects it has seen. The HDMI specification itself was not read.
source: HDMI Type D pin assignment from secondary sources (public pinout summaries and a cable-quality application note); the HDMI specification was not read. Engineering judgement.
consequence: JTAG programming and debug of a Frontend fail on any port used with a cable that lacks pin 2 (or pin 15).
suggested_action: Buy 'High Speed with Ethernet' cables and buzz pins 1, 2, 15, 17, 18 and 19 end to end on each cable type before use.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (interfaces note); the reviewer agrees with note.

title: About half the L3 LVDS pairs run 10-24 mm over L4 power islands, and B64_L6N runs 15.6 mm over an L4 gap.
what: The LVDS pairs on L3 sit 0.30 mm below a continuous ground plane on L2 and 0.42 mm above L4, a mixed power layer. A trace's return current flows in the nearest planes, so L2 gives every pair a clean path. On the L4 side, about half the clock and command pairs pass over 5 V power islands for 10-24 mm instead of ground, while the others see ground for their whole length or, for the SYNC pairs, only 3-4 mm of island. One line of the port 1 clock, B64_L6N, runs 15.6 mm over a gap in L4 while its partner stays over ground; at the recorded 32 MHz clock and 64 Mb/s this is harmless.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, L3 (In2), bank 64 LVDS pairs. Examples: B64_L18N 23.7 mm over PORT6_5V; B64_L1N 19.0 mm over PORT5_5V; B64_L9P 15.1 mm over FE_5V plus 2.8 mm over PORT7_5V; B64_L6N 15.6 mm over the PORT1_5V/DGND gap on L4, x about 71-89.6, y 142.8-145.7. Ground on L4 for the whole length: the command pairs of ports 1-6 (B64_L5, L3, L7, L15, L4, L2), B64_L6P and the port 6 clock B64_L8.
evidence: scratch/verify-hdmi-batch5/ref.py, output ref_out.txt: 0.05 mm sampling of L3 B64 tracks against the filled zones on L2 and L4. L2 voids only at each net's own via antipads, 0.7-1.4 mm per net. L4 non-ground length: L18N 23.73 mm, L18P 20.58 mm, L1N 19.01 mm, L9P 15.13 mm, L10N 12.87 mm, L24N 9.71 mm FE_5V + 5.61 mm VDCIN, L11/L13 about 16-17 mm, L19P 11.36 mm PORT2_5V + 10.64 mm void, L6N 15.62 mm void, L8N 0.31 mm; SYNC L16/L22/L23 3.2-4.1 mm. exports/hdmi/stackup.txt: L2-L3 core 0.30 mm, L3-L4 prepreg 2 x 0.2084 = 0.417 mm. gap.py: tracks 0.177 mm wide; minimum pair-to-pair edge gap 0.203 mm; gap inside each pair 0.191-0.200 mm. The V35 review's 3.6 % NEXT figure was not re-derived.
source: Engineering judgement
consequence: Slightly more common-mode noise and crosstalk on the affected clock and command lines. No effect at 64 Mb/s.
suggested_action: No change at the current rates. Re-check these return paths if the forwarded clock goes well above 125 MHz or the command rate above a few hundred Mb/s.
already_known: V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (LVDS bundles; L4 non-DGND for 0-24 mm; B64_L6N over the gap). The reviewer agrees: accept.

title: Board copper adds up to 176 ps port-to-port delay spread on command+SYNC pairs and 90 ps on separate SYNC.
what: SYNC goes to all eight head stacks, so any difference in path delay between ports becomes a timing difference between stacks. On this board the port-to-port spread is 176 ps on the command+SYNC pairs, 90 ps on the separate SYNC pairs and 165 ps on the clock pairs; if ports 3-6 use the separate SYNC and the other ports the SYNC folded into the command pair, the spread is about 189 ps. These are board-only numbers: vias, the XEM8310 module's internal routing and the cable lengths are not included and are not known. All are small against the 15.6 ns bit time.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, MC1 to J610-J617 through ESD parts U801-U816. Command+SYNC (pins 9/11): B64_L5, L3, L7, L15, L4, L2, L9, L21 for ports 1-8. Separate SYNC (pins 12/14, ports 3-6 only): B64_L16, L23, L22, L18. Clock (pins 6/8): B64_L6, L19, L13_GC, L11_GC, L1, L8, L10, L24.
evidence: Recomputed from exports/hdmi/board.json per net and layer at 7.07 ps/mm (L3 stripline) and 5.78 ps/mm (L1/L6). Command P leg, ports 1-8: 883.8, 848.2, 855.0, 841.1, 1010.0, 1016.8, 1000.9, 971.6 ps (port 4 120.2 mm, port 6 145.0 mm). Separate SYNC P: 811.8, 821.7, 888.7, 902.3 ps. Clocks 877 to 1042 ps. Clock minus command per port: +32.0, +43.6, +36.9, +35.8, +32.0, -32.4, +27.5, +7.8 ps. Mixed SYNC spread 812 to 1001 ps. Port map from exports/hdmi/pads.csv; SYNC use from inputs/hdmi/firmware_V34/fit_pins_V34_sync.xdc and inputs/notes/hdmi-cable-pin-map.md; fit_pins_V34.xdc says output timing is not yet defined.
source: Engineering judgement
consequence: No effect at a 15.6 ns bit time. It matters only if SYNC must line up between stacks to better than about 1 ns, and then the module and cable delays must be added.
suggested_action: Use these per-port numbers in the system SYNC budget together with cable lengths and XEM8310 trace lengths, or calibrate per-port delay in firmware.

title: DRC 0 does not check courtyards of 70 footprints or any pair skew, because those checks are off or undefined.
what: A courtyard is the keep-out outline KiCad uses to detect parts placed on top of each other. The project sets the missing_courtyard check to ignore, so 70 of the 312 footprints, which have no courtyard, are never overlap-checked; they include MC1-MC3, the PCIe edge J6, Y500, Q1, U2, U4, U5, U6 and the inherited BRK8310 passives. The custom rule file also sets no length, skew or uncoupled-length limit, so DRC 0 says nothing about pair matching. A separate check found no overlap and the cable LVDS pairs match within 1.42 mm, so nothing is wrong on V37, but DRC alone does not show it.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pro rule_severities; HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_dru. Footprints without a courtyard include MC1, MC2, MC3, J6, Y500, Q1, U2, U4, U5, U6, C5-C32, R2-R33, FB500-FB503, 7 fiducials, 10 test points and 2 unnamed items.
evidence: exports/hdmi/drc.json ignored_checks: missing_courtyard, track_not_centered_on_via, tuning_profile_track_geometries, footprint_filters_mismatch, footprint_type_mismatch; 0 violations, 0 unconnected, 0 parity. The .kicad_pro sets skew_out_of_range and length_out_of_range to error, but the .kicad_dru defines no such constraint (only width/gap, clearance, hole clearance, zone connection and disallow rules). pcbnew scan: 312 footprints, 70 without F.CrtYd/B.CrtYd. For the 51 real parts without a courtyard, pad plus fab/silk outline hits no other same-side pad. P/N mismatch from board.json: worst HDMI-cable LVDS pair B64_L11_GC 1.42 mm; larger mismatch only on non-cable header/resistor nets (B64_L20 18.5 mm, B64_L17 2.6 mm, B84/B86 2.6 mm). First review: PCIe at most 0.05 mm, recording at most 0.02 mm.
source: Engineering judgement
consequence: A later edit could place a part over a connector, or let a pair's skew grow, without DRC reporting it.
suggested_action: No change needed for V37. In the next revision, add courtyards to the inherited BRK8310 footprints and add diff-pair skew rules to the .kicad_dru (for example 0.1 mm for GT and PCIe pairs).

title: The right-hand U700 input and output capacitors reach PGND through vias to L2, not through top-side copper.
what: U700 is a TI TPSM63606 buck power module. TI asks for a symmetric pair of input and output capacitors, with their ground ends on local top-side copper tied to the module's PGND (power ground) pads, to keep the switching current loop small. The left-hand capacitors do this; the right-hand ones have their ground pads facing away from the module, on two separate top-side ground islands that reach PGND only through vias to the L2 plane. The solid L2 plane, short via paths and the module's internal 0402 input capacitors limit the effect.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, L1 (top). U700 PGND pins 17-20 at x 124.0; VIN1/VOUT1 at x 122.0, VIN2/VOUT2 at x 126.0. Right-hand C701/C703 (input) and C705/C707 (output), ground pads at x 128.175 on zones 'U700 PGND input east' and 'U700 PGND output east'. Left-hand C700/C702 and C704/C706 ground pads at x 123.275 in the centre PGND copper.
evidence: exports/hdmi/pads.csv: U700 pins 1/16 VIN at x 122.0/126.0, pins 8/9 VOUT at x 122.0/126.0, pins 17-20 PGND at x 124.0; C700-C707 pad 2 (DGND) at x 123.275 (left) and 128.175 (right). pcbnew union of L1 DGND zone fills, tracks and pads in x 115-135, y 45-75: centre piece 36.5 mm2 with 20 vias (x 121.3-126.7); east-input piece 15.4 mm2 with 6 vias (y 50-56.8); east-output piece 16.0 mm2 with 4 vias (y 61.9-70); the three are not joined on L1. Zone fills alone: 35.64, 15.29 and 15.06 mm2 (exports/hdmi/zones.csv).
source: TI TPSM63606 datasheet SLVSGB4B (Oct 2021, revised Apr 2022), section 11.1, p.31 (also section 8.2, p.17), https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tpsm63606.pdf
consequence: A slightly larger switching loop on the right-hand side and somewhat more EMI. The module's internal input capacitors carry most of the fastest current.
suggested_action: No change for V37. If the U700 area is reworked, mirror the four right-hand capacitors so their ground pads join the centre PGND copper.
already_known: V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md (si-power-layout note). The reviewer agrees: note.

title: The card is 2.95 mm taller than a full-height PCIe card and has no bracket, so it fits only an open adapter.
what: The board outline is copied unchanged from the BRK8310 reference. It is 2.95 mm taller than the PCIe full-height limit, measured from the tip of the card-edge fingers. The board has no holes for a metal mounting bracket, and port 8 sits outside the opening of a standard bracket. This matches the recorded decision to use the card only in an open adapter or riser.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, whole Edge.Cuts outline (x 64.676-232.326, y 47.954-162.054; finger tip at y 162.05); J617 (port 8, about y 52.8-55.4); mounting holes MH2/MH3.
evidence: The Edge.Cuts of boards/hdmi/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37.kicad_pcb and of the BRK8310 replica (Reference/BRK8310/KiCad_Original/BRK8310_Original_Layout/BRK8310_Replica_V4.kicad_pcb) have the same 22 segments. exports/hdmi/board.json: 167.65 mm long, 114.10 mm from finger tip to top edge. 114.10 - 111.15 (full-height maximum) = 2.95 mm. The length equals the half-length limit. exports/hdmi/parts.csv: only MH2/MH3 M3 standoff holes, no bracket holes. inputs/notes/hdmi-ext-v6-routing-handoff.md records the 5 Nov adapter-use decision and the removal of the bracket holes.
source: PCI Express Card Electromechanical Specification (CEM) Rev 3.0, Figs 9-1 and 9-3, as read in inputs/hdmi/V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 750-768 (the members-only CEM itself was not opened); 111.15 mm full-height figure from public card-size summaries.
consequence: The card will not fit a closed PC case, and the ports need hand support when cables are plugged in or pulled.

title: Four 4.7 uF 6.3 V 0402 capacitors on the FT232H 3.3 V rails run at 52 % of their rating and lose capacitance.
what: C507, C512, C513 and C515 are 4.7 uF, 6.3 V, X5R parts in the small 0402 size, on the 3.3 V rails of the FT232H USB chip. Ceramic X5R capacitors lose capacitance as the DC voltage across them rises (the DC-bias effect), and small parts lose the most. At 52 % of rating their real value is well below 4.7 uF; how far below was not taken from a maker curve. The FTDI datasheet gives no minimum capacitance, so the circuit should still work.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37: C507 and C512 on FTDI3V3 (the 3.3 V output of the FT232H regulator, U501 pin 39 VCCD, also feeding VCCIO pins 12/24/46), C513 on /FTDI3V3_PLL, C515 on /FTDI3V3_PHY. Part Taiyo Yuden JMK105BBJ475MV-F, LCSC C87147.
evidence: exports/hdmi/parts.csv and bom.csv: C507/C512/C513/C515 = JMK105BBJ475MV-F, X5R, 6.3 V, LCSC C87147 (one BOM line). LCSC product page C87147: 4.7 uF, 6.3 V, X5R, 0402. exports/hdmi/nets.csv: FTDI3V3 includes U501.39; C500 (4.7 uF 10 V) sits on /FTDI5V_FILTERED (VREGIN 5 V), so VCCD is a 3.3 V output. 3.3 / 6.3 = 0.524. No maker DC-bias curve was read, so the remaining capacitance is unquantified.
source: Engineering judgement; FTDI DS_FT232H, FT_000288 v1.82, section 6.1 (p. 52), from a copy fetched earlier (ftdichip.com refused access today); section text read, figure values not read.
consequence: The FT232H regulator output and the PLL/PHY filters have less bulk decoupling than the 4.7 uF value suggests.
suggested_action: No action needed now. If the BOM is changed, a 10 V 0402 or a 0603 part keeps more of its capacitance at 3.3 V.

title: No bottom-side polarized part is placed right under every reading of JLC's unpublished bottom-angle rule.
what: The placement file (CPL, the list of part positions and angles the factory's pick-and-place machine uses) gives each bottom part the angle 180 - KiCad angle + library offset. Under that reading, all 28 polarized bottom parts land on their pads when checked against JLC's own library footprints. JLC does not publish whether it flips a bottom part left-right or top-bottom, or which way it measures the angle, so the files cannot settle which reading the factory uses. Under one other reading the 18 parts at 90/270 deg are turned 180 deg; under another, those 18 are right but the other 10 are turned 180 deg. Only JLC's placement preview, or a written answer from JLC, settles it.
where: HDMI Extension Board V37, bottom side: D701-D708, U602, U603, U605, U610, U611-U618, U701-U708 (28 polarized parts); inputs/hdmi/V37_order/HDMI_Extension_Board_V37_CPL.csv.
evidence: scratch/hdmi-order/scripts/libangle.py, rerun on exports/hdmi/board.json and the V37 CPL: under the file's reading, worst pad error 0.04 mm (LEDs), 0.06 (U602), 0.01 (U603), 0.16 (U611-U618), 0.21 (U605, U701-U708), 0.16 (U610). Same flip axis, opposite angle direction: 1.54 mm (LEDs 180 deg off), 6.88 (U602), 2.97 (U603), 9.26 (U611-U618); U605/U610/U701-U708 unchanged. scratch/verify-hdmi-batch7/libangle4.py, flip top-to-bottom with the angle as written: the 18 parts correct, U605 and U701-U708 3.13 mm and U610 9.26 mm off (180 deg); the SOT-23-6 current-limit switches would sit reversed on symmetric pads. ORDER_NOTE_FOR_JLC_V37.md already has a pin-1 table for all 28 parts (for example D701 cathode at 108.20, -143.89, matching board.json pad 1, net D701-K).
source: JLCPCB help, 'Pick and place file for PCB assembly' (https://jlcpcb.com/help/article/pick-place-file-for-pcb-assembly): states only that positive angles are counter-clockwise, no bottom-side rule. JLC/EasyEDA library footprints for C94869, C4364118, C33002 and C443721 (easyeda.com API, 11 Nov 2026). KiBot position notes (https://kibot.readthedocs.io/en/latest/notes_position.html), as of Nov 2023.
consequence: If the factory uses a different reading and the preview is not checked, the port-fault LEDs or the current-limit and analog switches are fitted 180 deg turned.
suggested_action: Approve JLC's placement preview only after each of the 28 parts shows pin 1 or the cathode at the coordinates in the order note's pin-1 table, as the note already asks.
already_known: V35_prefab_review/ALL_FINDINGS.md lines 87 and 154 (bottom convention inferred, not from JLC documentation). The pin-1 table in the note mitigates it.

title: The V37 placement file and BOM were patched from the V35 files rather than regenerated from the V37 board.
what: The script that builds the V37 order files copies the V35 BOM byte for byte and overwrites 35 angles in the V35 placement file from a hard-coded table. It never reads the V37 board for positions, values or part numbers. Today the result matches the V37 board, so there is no error now. A later part move or part change would not reach the order files unless the script is changed, and the export script only prints position differences without stopping.
where: inputs/hdmi/V37_scripts/order37.py and export37.sh; inputs/hdmi/V37_order/ BOM and CPL.
evidence: order37.py reads HDMI_Extension_Board_V35_CPL.csv and copies HDMI_Extension_Board_V35_BOM.csv; its angle table has 35 entries. cmp: the V37 BOM is identical to ~/kicad_work/HDMI_V35/order/HDMI_Extension_Board_V35_BOM.csv; CPL columns 1-4 are identical to V35. scratch/verify-hdmi-batch7/cmp.py, CPL vs exports/hdmi/pos.csv: 270 rows each, 0 side differences, 10 position differences (the deliberate pad-centre rows J4, J500, J610-J617), 35 angle differences, all in the table. BOM vs exports/hdmi/parts.csv: 270 references each way, 0 LCSC conflicts; 35 fitted parts have no LCSC/JLCPCB field on the board (for example C5-C12, C27, C28, C31, C32, J4, Q1, R2). export37.sh prints a V35/V37 position diff but does not fail on it and ignores value or part-number changes.
source: Engineering judgement.
consequence: No error now. A later revision could ship stale positions, values or part numbers without any warning that stops the build.
suggested_action: For the next revision, add the missing LCSC fields to the 35 board parts, generate positions and BOM from the saved board, and apply the angle table on top.

title: The V3 enclosure has no known inside air temperature, and an estimate puts it 15-49 C or more above the room.
what: The enclosure V3 record says its thermal behaviour has not been simulated or measured. The box is closed, has no fan and has only 11 slots in the keel floor (the keel is the lower pocket that holds the Thunderbolt adapter), yet it also holds the XEM8310 and the adapter. The U700 heat sinks are described only as 'as V2'. The current U700 (the 5 V power module) can safely deliver falls as the inside air gets warmer, so the files cannot fix a U700 current budget for the box; only a measured box-air temperature can.
where: Enclosure V3 (inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md, 'Power' and 'Open points'); U700 at the J4 corner of the HDMI Extension Board V37.
evidence: inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md line 7 (thermal not verified) and line 62 (nothing simulated or measured; 11 floor slots; heat sinks as V2; no fan); box 184.1 x 139.7 x 34.4 mm plus a 136.5 x 34.8 x 48 mm keel, about 0.0949 m2 of wall; adapter 3-5 W. inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md section 2: XEM8310 10-15 W expected, 20 W high; U700 loses about 1-2.5 W. Heat kept inside about 14-28 W (port power leaves through the cables). With an assumed 6-10 W/m2K from wall to room: 14 / (10 x 0.0949) = 14.8 K to 28 / (6 x 0.0949) = 49.2 K wall rise; inside air is warmer still. The estimate ignores the connector and service windows and the floor slots, so the true rise may sit toward the low end. At 60 C box air and RthJA 33-38 C/W, allowed loss is 65/38 = 1.71 W to 65/33 = 1.97 W, about 4.95-5.3 A before U700 reaches 125 C (loss curve SLVSGB4B Fig. 7-10).
source: Engineering judgement; inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md; inputs/hdmi/power_estimate/START_HERE.md section 2; TI SLVSGB4B Fig. 7-10 (U700 loss curve).
consequence: Without a measured or simulated box-air temperature, the U700 current budget in the enclosure cannot be stated more tightly than the 40-60 C range used here.
suggested_action: Before relying on the 0.63-0.71 A per-port cases, run the board and XEM8310 in the printed box with a dummy 5 A FE_5V load and log the box air and U700 top temperature, or add a small fan or vents to the V3 concept.
already_known: inputs/hdmi/enclosure_V3/START_HERE.md lists 'Thermal' as an open point. The reviewer agrees it is open; no severity is recorded there.
